newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan Taleban use tank to destroy beer.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban use tank to destroy beer.

text.p: Afghanistan's purist Islamic Taleban used a heavy battle tank to crush hundreds of cans of beer on Thursday to demonstrate their loathing of alcohol.
The tank drove over the hoard a dozen times, sending streams of foam over bystanders as Taleban fighters pushed unbroken cans back under the tracks.

The demonstration left a large pool of beer -- mixed with the contents of a few cans of soda pop the Taleban seem to have misidentified -- in the road at the central Shar-a-Naw Square near the Iranian embassy.

Iranian diplomats are the only ones still resident in Kabul and it was not immediately clear whether the enmity between the Sunni Moslem Taleban and Shia Moslem Iran was a factor in the choice of site.

Iran has called the Taleban unIslamic for their stern implentation of Sharia law, including banning women from the work place and schools, and recognises the government the militia drove from Kabul a month ago.
It was the second time since then the Taleban have used a tank to destroy alcohol in Kabul, Afghanistan's most liberal city.
Last time, they chose a hill top on the outskirts of the capital to smash several hundred cases of alcohol seized from the Intercontinental Hotel, Kabul's only remaining large hotel.
On Thursday, the Taleban did not say specifically where the beer had come from, saying only it had been seized.
The Sunni and Shia are the two main groups of Islam: the Sunni are the orthodox majority while the Shia give weight mostly to the Koran and the interpretation of their theologians.
Religious leaders of both sects avow opposition to alcohol.
